title: I wonder what shes got like now after living with that dotty husband of hers she had her face beginning to look drawn and run down the last time I saw her she must have been just after a row with him because I saw on the moment she was edging to draw down a conversation about husbands and talk about him to run him down what was it she told me
html_source: Molly muses over Josie, a former interest of Bloom’s, who was mentioned earlier in the text too. In this perspective however, we see how Molly views Josie from a female perspective, in the role of a fellow wife. The morals here seem skewed, considering Molly’s own infidelity and the subtle hint of irritation and concern over Josie and Bloom’s interactions. It is also interesting to note how Molly still values her relationship with Bloom, considering herself lucky to be paired with her husband, and needed by him, while Josie is stuck with a “dotty husband” who wears her down. Most importantly, it is fascinating to read this text from a “female’s perspective” because its bluntness seems authentic, and her internal struggle to pretend there is a contentedness with Bloom as a means to excuse, or distance her jealous emotions towards Josie. She attempts to act in denial of her own feelings here to some degree, and yet she reverts back to her dissatisfaction soon enough, showing the realistic innerworkings of Molly. Joyce manages to capture a unique perspective whilst preserving the character development by simply ending the text with Molly ruminating once more on a memory of Bloom’s proposal to her, similar to how he ends this sentence with her preference and relief to be with Bloom, rather than with a potentially worse man such as Josie’s husband.
